No storms this week for Punctual Pros

There are no storms in this week's data. The National Weather Service shows zero active alerts across PA, NJ and the New England states, and the forecast for the six hubs shown is dry. This week's demand should track the normal October seasonal pattern, not a weather spike (National Weather Service alerts; Open-Meteo 7-day forecast).

What the forecast shows

  • No rain. Precipitation is 0.0 in. at all six hubs shown from Oct 6 to Oct 10, 2026. Chance of rain is 0–1%.
  • Breezy, not stormy. Gusts peak on Oct 8, 2026, then ease to 8–21 mph by Oct 10.
  • Cool nights. Lows near 40°F on Oct 7, 2026, then highs in the low 70s.
  • Fog at Lebanon on Oct 8 (weather code 45). It does not affect demand.
  • Four of ten hubs are not shown. Their conditions are unconfirmed.

Expected effect on calls

  • Weather effect: probably none (est.). The model raises expected calls only when a weather multiplier is active. Dry, mild days with these gusts are unlikely to trigger one. The trigger thresholds are not in the extract, so this is an inference (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • Seasonality matters more. Nationally, October is the busiest HVAC month because of heating start-ups (Samsara telematics, via the Punctual Pros demand model). The near-40°F nights may bring early no-heat and start-up calls (est.).
  • Off-hours load is lighter. Off-hours share of inbound calls was 9.8% in October 2025, versus 14.1% in June (ServiceTitan, via the Punctual Pros demand model).
  • Baselines are market-wide. The model uses 10 HVAC, 16 plumbing and 7 electrical calls per day per 10k households. These cover all providers, not Punctual Pros alone. Punctual Pros market share is an unknown parameter, so its call volume cannot be stated from this context (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • Storm history adds nothing here. The storm events dataset is a historical record of damaging weather. It shows nothing for this week, and by its own caveat it should not drive temperature-related HVAC forecasts (Punctual Pros storm events).

What would sharpen this

  • Punctual Pros booked calls by trade and day for Oct 2026, from ServiceTitan or the CRM.
  • The weather-multiplier thresholds and the October monthly index from the full model.
  • Forecasts for the four hubs not shown.

Next actions

  1. Pull Punctual Pros booked calls for Oct 6–10, 2026 by trade. Compare them with the October baseline to check for a heating start-up lift.
  2. Weight dispatch toward daytime HVAC start-up and no-heat capacity rather than storm coverage. Off-hours demand is seasonally low.
  3. Load 12+ months of booked-call history so the model's assumed multipliers can be replaced with fitted ones.
  4. Confirm the remaining four hub forecasts before the weekend staffing call.

This week's demand should track the normal October seasonal pattern, not a weather spike (National Weather Service alerts; Open-Meteo 7-day forecast).

## What the forecast shows

- **No rain.** Precipitation is 0.0 in. at all six hubs shown from Oct 6 to Oct 10, 2026. Chance of rain is 0–1%.
- **Breezy, not stormy.** Gusts peak on Oct 8, 2026, then ease to 8–21 mph by Oct 10.

## Expected effect on calls

- **Weather effect: probably none (est.).** The model raises expected calls only when a weather multiplier is active. Dry, mild days with these gusts are unlikely to trigger one. The trigger thresholds are not in the extract, so this is an inference (Punctual Pros demand model).
- **Seasonality matters more.** Nationally, October is the busiest HVAC month because of heating start-ups (Samsara telematics, via the Punctual Pros demand model). The near-40°F nights may bring early no-heat and start-up calls (est.).
- **Off-hours load is lighter.** Off-hours share of inbound calls was 9.8% in October 2025, versus 14.1% in June (ServiceTitan, via the Punctual Pros demand model).
- **Baselines are market-wide.** The model uses 10 HVAC, 16 plumbing and 7 electrical calls per day per 10k households. These cover all providers, not Punctual Pros alone. Punctual Pros market share is an unknown parameter, so its call volume cannot be stated from this context (Punctual Pros demand model).
- **Storm history adds nothing here.** The storm events dataset is a historical record of damaging weather. It shows nothing for this week, and by its own caveat it should not drive temperature-related HVAC forecasts (Punctual Pros storm events).

## What would sharpen this

- Punctual Pros booked calls by trade and day for Oct 2026, from ServiceTitan or the CRM.
- The weather-multiplier thresholds and the October monthly index from the full model.
- Forecasts for the four hubs not shown.

## Next actions

1. Pull Punctual Pros booked calls for Oct 6–10, 2026 by trade. Compare them with the October baseline to check for a heating start-up lift.
2. Weight dispatch toward daytime HVAC start-up and no-heat capacity rather than storm coverage. Off-hours demand is seasonally low.
3. Load 12+ months of booked-call history so the model's assumed multipliers can be replaced with fitted ones.
4. Confirm the remaining four hub forecasts before the weekend staffing call.
